text.p: French holding company Compagnie Generale d'Industrie et de Participations (CGIP) expects higher pre-exceptional results this year and big exceptional gains as well, chairman Ernest-Antoine Seilliere said in a newspaper interview on Monday.
Seilliere also told Le Figaro that CGIP would consider offers from Daimler Benz AG or another group for its stake in computer systems house Cap Gemini.
CGIP recently sold four percent of Cap Gemini and holds 20 percent.
"(Results for 1996) will be exceptional because of the capital gains from the sales of Crown Cork & Seal and Cap Gemini," Seilliere said.
"Profit excluding exceptionals will also be higher thanks to a strong contribution from Cap Gemini and improvements at BioMerieux Alliance, Wheelabrator-Allevard and Orange-Nassau," he said.

CGIP recently sold half its stake in Crown Cork to finance the purchase of around 20 percent of car parts manufacturer Valeo from Cerus. He said he considers Valeo has prospects for both external and internal growth.
Although Valeo has achieved a critical mass in some of its businesses, it still needs to grow some of its activities, such as wipers and car interior components, he said.

As for Cap Gemini, Seilliere said: "We don't exclude a proposal from Daimler Benz for the 20 percent in Cap Gemini that we own, and we would respond favourably if the conditions were right and if they were not so in coming."

He said Cap Gemini had international expansion ambitions and CGIP did not have the means "to accompany it in such projects. If Cap Gemini, on the other hand, remains concentrated in Europe, we could remain a shareholder".
Seilliere said the group would also be open to other offers for its Cap Gemini stake. "We're not locked in with Daimler Benz," he added.

Seilliere said CGIP had no immediate plans for a capital increase but would be willing at some point to discuss it with its shareholders and Marine-Wendel, the main shareholder of CGIP which Seilliere also heads.
